title: Open model vetting + runtime-fit walkthrough - Pioneer HealthTech
summary: Intro + demo of model catalog, bench artifacts, and runtime compatibility. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment, and security requirements (SOC2, KMS). Agreed next steps: share micro-bench spreadsheet, run a 48h sample bench on Pioneer data subset, and set up a Private deployment scoping call.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Security: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC 2
action_items: Alex Morgan: Share micro-bench spreadsheet and sample JSON payloads - due 2026-11-06
Priya Shah: Schedule 48h sample bench on Redwood hosted infra with Pioneer data subset - due 2026-11-09
Mark Reynolds / Pioneer: Provide security questionnaire answers and trusted IP ranges - due 2026-11-10
next_steps: AE to send pricing tier + pilot terms
SE to run targeted bench and upload raw logs to shared drive
Schedule follow-up scoping call for Private deployment (include network/security team)
transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-11-02 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Pioneer CTO), Tom Hsu (Pioneer ML), Mark Reynolds (Pioneer Security)

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round of intros, and then we'll jump into the catalog walkthrough. Lena, Tom, Mark, thanks for carving out time.
[00:12] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Yeah thanks Alex, excited - we are trying to validate open model candidates for our clinical summarization pipeline, and wanna understand runtime fit.
[00:20] Tom Hsu: Hi, yeah my role is ML infra, so I'm especially interested in latency, GPU selection, and how the KV cache works across sessions.
[00:29] Mark Reynolds: And I'll be looking at encryption, audit logs, and basically whether we can get an on-prem footprint or VPC to satisfy compliance.
[00:36] Priya (SE): Great. quick agenda: 1) catalog search and filters for task/accuracy/cost, 2) micro-bench results and how to read them, 3) compatibility matrix -> kernel mapping, 4) deployment options and security. we'll keep it interactive.
[00:50] Alex: One quick note — I'll be sharing a micro-bench spreadsheet after the call with sample payloads you can run.

[01:10] Priya: Ok pulling up the catalog — you can see we have model cards with task-fit tags. if you search "clinical-summarization" or "long-context" it returns curated picks. some OCR in the UI might show model names differently in the transcript — e.g., 'Lumen-13B' shows up as 'Lumon 13 B' sometimes in automated notes.
[01:33] Tom: Are these scores based on your internal evals? do you expose the raw prompts?
[01:38] Priya: Yes, each entry links to bench results (we call them micro-bench and bench-sprint artifacts). there's a raw bench CSV and an interpreted signal sheet — latency median/p95, quality metrics (ROUGE, F1 variants for extractive tasks), and token-cost. sometimes the automatic transcript will swap ROUGE for 'rouge oh' in notes — ignore that.

[02:10] Alex: Let's demo a shortlist. I'm going to add three open models to a compare view: 'Beacon-7B', 'Helios-13B-quant', and 'Atlas-11B-int8' — quick disclaimer: some of our model labels map to several runtime variants (CPU-friendly half-precision, GPU int8, AVX-optimized).
[02:32] Dr. Lena Ortiz: For clinical data, we need high recall on critical findings. we can accept a bit more latency if it improves recall.
[02:42] Priya: Noted. I'll highlight the quality vs latency scatter chart — on the left we have per-token cost, on the top the quality signal. Beacon-7B sits low-latency/low-cost but slightly lower on recall. Atlas-11B-int8 shows better recall but needs a specific kernel path for best p95.

[03:15] Tom: Kernel path? can you say more — like which CUDA / Triton / XLA kernels?
[03:21] Priya: Sure — our runtime picks kernels by model architecture and length distribution. Atlas-11B-int8 wants grouped GEMM kernels and a fused attention kernel; we map that to the 'A100-1x' profile or 'H100-2x' to hit target latency. if you're on <A100 class hardware, you'll see a p95 bump. sometimes our notes say 'gem-k' or 'gem e-k' — that's a transcription hiccup for 'grouped GEMM'.

[04:05] Alex: Here's the compatibility matrix view — rows are model families, columns are hardware profiles and runtime features (KV cache, continuous batching, prefix caching). green means verified, yellow experimental, red unsupported.
[04:21] Mark: I see a Private column — what does that mean exactly? we need to know ROE for VPC and key management.
[04:29] Priya: Private means the customer-managed control plane option: you run the inference pods inside your VPC or on-prem cluster, Redwood control plane can be air-gapped if needed, and we provide connectors for KMS/HSM. note: some transcripts show 'KMS/HSM' as 'K-M-S H-M-S' which is harmless.

[05:10] Tom: For the bench run, what's your sample size? we need to include longer docs, sometimes 8k to 32k tokens.
[05:18] Priya: Micro-bench typically uses 50-100 representative prompts with length buckets (512, 2048, 8192). For long-context, we run additional sequence-length sweeps. we'll replicate your 32k doc subset in the 48h sample bench.

[05:50] Dr. Lena Ortiz: On data residency: our dataset contains PHI. we cannot send raw PHI to hosted vendors without BAA. do you support BAAs and on-prem?
[05:59] Alex: Yes we have enterprise options: Dedicated capacity with contractual isolation, and Private which is customer-hosted. We can engage legal — I'll share our security pack and SOC 2 evidence.

[06:25] Mark: On audit logs — do you surface token-level logs or redacted interactions? we need to show lineage for compliance audits.
[06:33] Priya: We provide configurable retention and redaction rules. you can choose token-level diagnostics for the bench run but have them redact PHI in production. Redwood Console gives per-route traces and exportable audit logs. sometimes the transcript tool says 'route traces' as 'road traces' — obvious error.

[07:05] Alex: jumping back to the catalog — i'm going to open the bench detail for Helios-13B-quant. see this pane: runtime variants, quantization profile (int8, int4 experimental), and the kernel mapping. Helios had an int8 path that needed a custom fused attention kernel which we shipped in v2.3 runtime. older runtimes will use a fallback slower path.
[07:33] Tom: Cool. what's the expected cost delta between int8 and fp16 for a 1M token month?
[07:38] Priya: Rough ballpark: int8 can be 30-45% lower per-token on compatible hardware because of smaller memory bandwidth and higher throughput. fp16 is more predictable across hardware but more expensive. we'll include per-token cost estimates in the micro-bench sheet.

[08:10] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Are there recommended models for extraction + hallucination suppression? we've had hallucination on long clinical notes.
[08:18] Priya: We flag models with low hallucination risk from our evals. also, you can enable reranker or grounded inference tool calls — Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured outputs to reduce hallucination. sometimes our automated notes call that 'function calling' or 'tool call' interchangeably.

[09:00] Alex: i'm going to show routing policies — you can configure by latency SLO, cost budget, or accuracy. you can pin a primary model and set a cheaper fallback if latency exceeds X ms. plus region-aware routing for data residency.
[09:20] Tom: Will fallback preserve session KV cache? if we route to a smaller variant, context windows differ.
[09:28] Priya: Good question — fallbacks can either be stateless or we can map KV caches between compatible variants if you use the same architecture family. if incompatible, session reconstruction is needed, which increases latency. sometimes notes will say 'K-V cash' which is K-V cache.

[10:00] Mark: For Private deployments, do you provide the runtime images and an ops playbook?
[10:07] Priya: Yes we provide OCI images, Helm charts, and an ops runbook. we'll also provide kernel recommendations per GPU SKU. the playbook includes test harness for the bench.

[11:05] Alex: Let's look at a real bench artifact for Pioneer-like input. opening a bench CSV — here are per-request latencies with p50/p95, GPU memory, and token throughput. note the p95 spike at sequence length 8192 for Beacon-7B; that's the tail we worry about.
[11:30] Tom: Does your bench capture warm vs cold cache? we saw 2x difference when KV cache was cold.
[11:36] Priya: We include warmup runs and measure cold-start vs steady-state. KV cache warmup is in the artifact notes.

[12:10] Dr. Lena Ortiz: pricing — if we do a pilot on hosted vs dedicated, how do we model costs?
[12:18] Alex: We provide a pilot pricing model: hosted per-token pricing with a credit allowance for bench runs, Dedicated has a reserved capacity commit with predictable unit economics; Private has a platform fee plus support. i'll send a sample TCO spreadsheet.

[13:00] Tom: Are there any caveats about quantization and accuracy drop for clinical language?
[13:07] Priya: Yes — we annotate accuracy deltas for each quant profile in the bench sheet. int4 is experimental for many LLMs and may increase hallucination; we recommend int8 as first pass.

[14:10] (short silence / crosstalk)
[14:25] Alex: Quick recap — we'll run a 48h sample bench with your 50 doc subset, run long-context sweeps up to 32k, and share results and kernel mapping.

[14:40] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Great. also want to involve legal/security early — Mark, can you collect the questionnaire?
[14:46] Mark Reynolds: Yep I'll consolidate and reply by next week.

[15:00] Tom: One more technical nit — do you support multi-node KV cache for cross-GPU sessions? we have some flows that exceed single GPU memory.
[15:08] Priya: We do experimental sharded KV across nodes in Dedicated and Private. caveat: it adds cross-node latency, but it enables >32k contexts. we can include that in the bench.

[16:00] Alex: ok we're about halfway; any other must-discuss items?
[16:05] Dr. Lena Ortiz: I want to make sure we get a clear migration path from your hosted bench to our Private deployment if we choose that route.
[16:12] Priya: We'll produce a migration plan: config differences, networking, and a runbook to replay bench traces.

[17:30] (Priya walks through console UI showing per-route trace and rollout policy)
[18:05] Priya: note the rollout control where you can do a 10% canary to dedicated and auto-fallback to hosted if the dedicated pool falls below capacity. that was recently improved; if the transcript says 'canary to decayed' that's wrong, it's 'dedicated'.

[19:00] Tom: For the sample bench run, can you surface raw model outputs (redacted) so our clinical team can score hallucinations?
[19:08] Alex: Yes, we'll share redacted outputs and the scoring sheet.

[20:00] Dr. Lena Ortiz: timeline — we're targeting a pilot decision by end of month.
[20:06] Alex: Sounds doable if we start bench this week.

[21:00] (discussion of contract terms, SLA)
[22:30] Mark: do you have a standard BAA?
[22:35] Alex: yes, we'll attach the BAA and security pack.

[23:40] Priya: Final note on compatibility matrix: we maintain per-model-per-runtime-version verification. when you see 'experimental' it means we have partial kernel support and recommend a bench. the automated transcript may render 'experimental' as 'experi mental' sometimes.

[24:55] Alex: Closing — recap of action items and due dates: micro-bench sheet (Alex), bench run (Priya), security questionnaire (Mark). we'll set follow-up for next Tuesday.

[25:12] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone. good walkthrough — looking forward to the bench.

[25:20] (call ends)

Notes about transcription: A few product names and kernel terms may be misrecognized in the automated transcript (e.g., grouped GEMM -> 'gem-k', 'K-V cache' -> 'K-V cash'). There was brief crosstalk around 14:10-14:25 that slightly garbled speaker labels.
